title_en: Wang Qinjie v. Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Guo Ruixing, et al. — dispute over private lending
ruling_gist_en: Under the subscribed capital system, after a company's debt arises, if the company extends the shareholders' capital contribution deadline by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting (or general meeting) or other means, and the creditor, on the ground that the company is unable to repay due debts, requests that the shareholders whose capital contribution deadline has not yet arrived under the amended term bear supplementary compensation liability for the company's unpaid debts within the scope of their unpaid capital contributions, the people's court shall support such request.
keywords_en: Civil; Private lending dispute; First instance; Basic People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Natural person; Legal person; Company Law; Supplementary compensation liability after extension of shareholder capital contribution period; Determination of private lending relationship; Validity of debt transfer; Partial support; Private lending; Subscribed capital system; Extension of shareholder capital contribution period; Private lending dispute, Guo Ruixing et al.
full_text_en:
Wang Qinjie (ONG KHIM KIAT) v. Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Guo Ruixing, et al. — Dispute over Private Lending

[Ruling Summary]

Under the system of subscribed capital contribution, where a company, after incurring a debt, extends the capital contribution period of its shareholders through a shareholders' (general) meeting resolution or other means, and the creditor claims that the company is unable to repay its due debts and requests that the shareholders whose capital contribution period has not yet expired under the revised terms bear supplementary compensation liability for the company's unsatisfied debts to the extent of their uncapitalized contributions, the people's court shall support such claims.

Plaintiff: Wang Qinjie (ONG KHIM KIAT), male, born April 11, 1948, national of the Republic of Indonesia, contact address: Pudong New Area, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.

Defendant: Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zhennan Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.
Legal representative: Qu Yibo (formerly known as Qu Pupu), executive director of the company.

Defendant: Guo Ruixing, female, born March 17, 1991, Han Chinese, domiciled at: Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Defendant: Qu Yibo (formerly known as Qu Pupu), male, born January 30, 1987, Han Chinese, domiciled at: Yanshi City, Henan Province, People's Republic of China.

Third Party: Cai Litao, male, born December 19, 1966, Han Chinese, domiciled at: Jianxi District, Luoyang City, Henan Province, People's Republic of China.

The plaintiff, Wang Qinjie (ONG KHIM KIAT), filed an action with the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Licheng Company"), Guo Ruixing, Qu Yibo, and the third party Cai Litao, concerning a dispute over private lending.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On December 30, 2015, the plaintiff and the defendant Licheng Company entered into a "Management Consulting Service Agreement." The main terms of the Agreement provided that Licheng Company, in the name of management, borrowed RMB 1,000,000 from Wang Qinjie at an annual interest rate of 15%, with the loan term from December 30, 2015, to December 29, 2016. After the agreement was signed, Wang Qinjie transferred RMB 1,000,000 to Licheng Company on December 30, 2015, as agreed. However, upon the maturity of the loan, Licheng Company failed to repay the principal and interest as agreed. Licheng Company's conduct infringed upon Wang Qinjie's legitimate rights and interests. The defendants Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo are shareholders of Licheng Company. After the subscribed capital contribution period expired, they failed to fully pay up their registered capital and should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the above debt of Licheng Company. Accordingly, Wang Qinjie filed this lawsuit, requesting that the court order (1) Licheng Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 1,000,000 (hereinafter in the same currency) and pay interest calculated at an annual rate of 15% on the principal of RMB 1,000,000 from December 30, 2015, until the date of actual repayment; and (2) Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo to bear joint and several liability for Licheng Company's repayment obligations.

Defendant Licheng Company's Defense: 1. According to the Management Consulting Service Agreement, Licheng Company was an intermediary for the loan, and the actual borrower was a third party, Zheng Moumou. There was no lending relationship between the plaintiff Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company. Licheng Company only assumed a guaranty liability for Zheng Moumou's debt. However, when Wang Qinjie claimed the guaranty liability from Licheng Company, the guaranty period had already expired, so Licheng Company should not bear any liability. 2. If it is held that there was a lending relationship between Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company, Licheng Company had already repaid RMB 350,000 of the principal to Wang Qinjie through witness Ge Moumou. Furthermore, a debt transfer agreement was reached among Wang Qinjie, Licheng Company, and Cai Litao, whereby Licheng Company transferred the remaining outstanding principal of RMB 650,000 and corresponding interest to Cai Litao. Therefore, Wang Qinjie should claim from the third party Cai Litao. 3. The prerequisite for shareholders to bear liability is that the company is unable to repay its debts. Since this case is still under trial, it is uncertain whether the company can repay. Moreover, the shareholders' capital contribution liability is a separate legal relationship and should not be dealt with together in this case. 4. Cai Litao provided jadeite jewelry as a pledge to secure the loan to Wang Qinjie. Wang Qinjie should negotiate with Cai Litao or auction the pledged property upon the expiry of the security period; otherwise, there would be double recovery.

Facts Found by the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance:

On December 30, 2015, the plaintiff Wang Qinjie (Party A, lender) and the defendant Licheng Company (Party C, service provider) entered into a "Management Consulting Service Agreement." The Agreement did not specify the details of Party B (i.e., the borrower); only the name seal of Zheng Moumou was affixed at the signature section of the contract. The main terms of the Agreement provided: 2.1 Party A and Party B have capital needs and investment needs, and through Party C's intermediary introduction and assistance in handling relevant matters, the lending period, repayment method, amount, and expected return for Party A are as follows: Lending method: Chengfeng Nianxiang; lending amount: RMB 1,000,000; annualized interest rate: 15%; lending start and end dates: December 30, 2015, to December 29, 2016; interest distribution method: for monthly interest distribution products, the interest distribution date is the corresponding day of each month following the initial lending date; maturity principal and interest payment method: principal and all interest to be paid on the maturity date; 3.1 Party A shall remit the funds by bank transfer or third-party payment to the account designated by Party B or the designated bank escrow account within the agreed time, and interest shall accrue from the date of remittance; 4.1 Party B provides collateral as security for the loan, and the valuation of the collateral shall be specified in a separate agreement. The collateral shall go through the mortgage or pledge procedures in the name of Party C. In the event of Party B's default, Party C shall bear joint and several liability, undertake the obligation to advance payment, and be responsible for the disposal and distribution of proceeds from the collateral, and initiate legal proceedings to ensure the recovery of Party A's principal and interest; 7.2 Party C shall ensure the authenticity of the borrower and loan information provided by it, and there shall be no false or forged information. If Party A's interests are damaged as a result, Party C shall bear joint and several liability; 7.5 During the existence of the lending relationship between the lender and the borrower, if the borrower commits a default, Party C shall bear joint and several liability, safeguard Party A's legitimate rights and interests, and actively assist Party A in collecting and recovering from Party B. Once Party B is unable to pay or fails to pay Party A's principal and interest in a timely manner, Party A may transfer the creditor's rights to Party C in accordance with the law, and Party C shall make the payment on behalf of Party B.

On the same day, the plaintiff Wang Qinjie paid RMB 1,000,000 to the defendant Licheng Company, and Licheng Company issued a receipt to Wang Qinjie. After receiving the funds, Licheng Company did not actually lend them to Zheng Moumou.

After the agreed loan term in the Management Consulting Service Agreement expired, the plaintiff Wang Qinjie, having not received the loan principal and interest, negotiated with the defendant Licheng Company. Licheng Company instructed its former employee Ge Moumou to repay RMB 350,000 to Wang Qinjie. Ge Moumou remitted RMB 100,000, RMB 100,000, and RMB 150,000 to Wang Qinjie's bank account on February 14, 2017, February 17, 2017, and October 2, 2017, respectively. Witness Ge Moumou testified that when repaying Wang Qinjie, he stated that the RMB 350,000 was the loan principal repaid by Licheng Company.

On November 22, 2017, the third party Cai Litao (Party A, debtor, borrower) and the plaintiff Wang Qinjie (Party B, creditor, lender) entered into a "Pledge Agreement on Tangible Property," which mainly stipulated: Party A shall repay Party B the loan principal of RMB 650,000 and corresponding interest, and shall provide the items listed in the appendix (jadeite jewelry) as pledge collateral to secure Party B's rights and interests in the event that Party A is unable to repay the principal and interest due within the agreed time; the tangible property pledged under this agreement is jadeite jewelry, and the detailed list is shown in the appendix photos, totaling eleven pieces, serving as collateral for this loan; this contract is made in duplicate, with each of Party A and Party B holding one copy. After the Pledge Agreement was signed, Cai Litao delivered the pledged property to Wang Qinjie. As for whether the delivered property matched the description in the appendix, Wang Qinjie did not clarify in this case. During the trial, Wang Qinjie and the defendant Licheng Company each submitted an original copy of the Pledge Agreement. In the original copy provided by the plaintiff, Cai Litao signed as the borrower and Wang Qinjie signed as the lender. In the original copy submitted by Licheng Company, in addition to the signatures of Cai Litao and Wang Qinjie, there were also handwritten words "agree to this debt transfer" in the blank space, and the company seal of Licheng Company was affixed on that text.

Separately, it was found that the defendant Licheng Company is a limited liability company established on November 6, 2015, with a registered capital of RMB 50,000,000. The shareholders are the defendant Qu Yibo (subscribed capital contribution: RMB 25,500,000, capital contribution date: December 31, 2018, shareholding ratio: 51%) and the defendant Guo Ruixing (subscribed capital contribution: RMB 24,500,000, capital contribution date: December 31, 2018, shareholding ratio: 49%). Qu Yibo serves as the executive director, and Guo Ruixing serves as the supervisor.

Opinion of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance:

The issues in dispute at first instance were: 1. The legal relationship between the plaintiff Wang Qinjie and the defendant Licheng Company; 2. The nature of the Pledge Agreement on Tangible Property; 3. The nature of the RMB 350,000 paid by Ge Moumou.

1. Regarding the legal relationship between the plaintiff Wang Qinjie and the defendant Licheng Company.

The plaintiff Wang Qinjie argued that the relationship was one of lending, while the defendant Licheng Company argued that it was a guaranty relationship. First, although the Management Consulting Service Agreement formally involved three parties—the lender, the borrower, and the service provider—the identity of the borrower was unclear, and Licheng Company admitted that after receiving the RMB 1,000,000 from Wang Qinjie, it did not actually remit the funds to the borrower. Therefore, the court of first instance held that the contracting parties of the Agreement were Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company. Second, the substantive terms of the Agreement provided for a fixed lending amount, fixed annualized return, repayment of principal and interest at maturity, etc. Although styled as a service agreement, it was in essence a private lending agreement. In summary, the legal relationship between Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company was one of lending. Licheng Company's argument that it was only a guarantor and that Wang Qinjie's claim for it to bear guaranty liability had exceeded the guaranty period was untenable.

2. Regarding the nature of the Pledge Agreement on Tangible Property.

The plaintiff Wang Qinjie argued that the third party Cai Litao voluntarily assumed Licheng Company's repayment obligation, constituting an accession to debt. The defendant Licheng Company argued that Cai Litao replaced Licheng Company in repaying the debt, constituting a debt transfer. The court of first instance held that both Wang Qinjie and Cai Litao held original copies of the Pledge Agreement, and the contents of the two copies should be identical. However, compared with the copy held by Wang Qinjie, the copy held by Cai Litao and submitted by Licheng Company contained additional handwritten words "agree to this debt transfer" and the seal of Licheng Company in the blank space. The court of first instance held that if such content was indeed the consensus of the parties at the time of signing the Pledge Agreement, it should have appeared in both copies. Since the above words and seal only appeared in the agreement held by Cai Litao, the court was inclined to believe that it was unilaterally added later. Therefore, the content of the Pledge Agreement should be determined based on the original copy held by Wang Qinjie. Accordingly, Licheng Company's claim that a consensus on debt transfer had been reached among Wang Qinjie, Licheng Company, and Cai Litao could not be established. Furthermore, during the proceedings, Wang Qinjie explicitly stated that he would not make a claim against Cai Litao in this case. Therefore, the pledge matters involved in the Pledge Agreement are not within the scope of this case. If Wang Qinjie or Cai Litao believe their rights and interests have been harmed, they may file separate lawsuits.

3. Regarding the nature of the RMB 350,000 paid by Ge Moumou.

The plaintiff Wang Qinjie argued that the RMB 350,000 should not be considered as repayment by the defendant Licheng Company, or if it were deemed as such, it should first be applied to offset interest. Licheng Company argued that the RMB 350,000 paid by Ge Moumou should be recognized as repayment of principal. The court of first instance held that the Pledge Agreement was signed after Ge Moumou's repayment and provided for the repayment of the loan principal of RMB 650,000 and corresponding interest. This principal amount exactly matched the outstanding loan principal owed by Licheng Company to Wang Qinjie after deducting the amount repaid by Ge Moumou. This indicated that when signing the Pledge Agreement, Wang Qinjie acknowledged the RMB 350,000 as repayment of the loan principal by Licheng Company. The testimony of witness Ge Moumou also corroborated the above facts. Therefore, the court of first instance held that the RMB 350,000 repayment constituted the loan principal repaid by Licheng Company to Wang Qinjie.

In summary, a private lending relationship existed between the plaintiff Wang Qinjie and the defendant Licheng Company. Wang Qinjie had performed its contractual obligation to lend RMB 1,000,000 to Licheng Company as agreed. Licheng Company only repaid RMB 350,000 in principal, constituting a breach of contract. It should bear the legal liability to repay the remaining principal of RMB 650,000 and corresponding interest. The corresponding interest shall be calculated in stages based on the actually outstanding principal amount. The defendants Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo, as shareholders of Licheng Company, failed to fully pay up their capital contributions after the subscribed capital contribution period expired, constituting a failure to perform or fully perform their capital contribution obligations. They should bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of Licheng Company's debts that cannot be satisfied, within the scope of the principal and interest of their respective uncapitalized contributions. During the trial, Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo, having been lawfully summoned by the court, failed to appear without justification, which constitutes a disregard for the law and shall be deemed as waiving their rights to defense, cross-examination, and other litigation rights, and they shall also bear certain legal consequences.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 41 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, Articles 196, 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 29, Paragraph 2, Item (2) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases, Article 13, Paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai rendered its judgment on June 28, 2019:

1. The defendant Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days of the effective date of this judgment, repay the plaintiff Wang Qinjie the loan principal of RMB 650,000;
2. The defendant Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days of the effective date of this judgment, pay the plaintiff Wang Qinjie interest of RMB 247,750 for the period from December 30, 2015, to October 2, 2017, and interest from October 3, 2017, to the date of actual repayment (calculated at an annual rate of 15% on the principal of RMB 650,000);
3. The defendant Guo Ruixing shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of the payment obligations set forth in items 1 and 2 above of the defendant Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. that cannot be satisfied, within the scope of the principal and interest of the uncapitalized contribution of RMB 24,500,000;
4. The defendant Qu Yibo shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of the payment obligations set forth in items 1 and 2 above of the defendant Shanghai Licheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. that cannot be satisfied, within the scope of the principal and interest of the uncapitalized contribution of RMB 25,500,000;
5. The remaining claims of the plaintiff Wang Qinjie are dismissed.

Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court.

Grounds of Appeal by Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing: 1. The first instance failed to include an important party, Wang Mouyu. As the former sole shareholder and former debtor of Licheng Company, Wang Mouyu participated in signing the Pledge Agreement on Tangible Property and was an important party in this case. Although Wang Mouyu's signature did not appear on the Pledge Agreement, he participated in the execution of the agreement. The debts involved in this case arose during the period when Wang Mouyu was the former shareholder of Licheng Company. The words "agree to this debt transfer" on the Pledge Agreement held by the first-instance third party Cai Litao were written by Wang Mouyu. 2. The first instance failed to clearly ascertain the identity of Cai Litao in the Management Consulting Service Agreement and the Pledge Agreement. Cai Litao was in fact the debtor under the Pledge Agreement and the actual user of the funds under the Management Consulting Service Agreement. 3. The first instance did not determine the nature of the Pledge Agreement. Given that the parties disputed its nature, it was inappropriate for the first instance to hold that the agreement was not within the scope of this case. 4. The first instance failed to correctly ascertain the capital contribution period for Guo Ruixing and the first-instance defendant Qu Yibo. The deadline for the subscribed capital contribution should be November 4, 2045, as indicated by the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Since the capital contribution period has not yet expired, Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo should not bear liability for Licheng Company's debts. Therefore, they requested that the first-instance judgment be set aside and either Wang Qinjie's first-instance claims be dismissed or the case be remanded for retrial. The litigation costs of the first and second instances should be borne by Wang Qinjie.

Appellee Wang Qinjie's Response: The first instance correctly ascertained the facts and applied the law. He disagreed with the appellants Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing's appeal requests. 1. The Management Consulting Service Agreement was signed between Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company, not between Wang Qinjie and the legal representative of Licheng Company in his personal capacity. Therefore, a change in the legal representative does not affect the rights and obligations of the parties. 2. Wang Qinjie's lawsuit is based on the Management Consulting Service Agreement, which has no direct causal relationship with the Pledge Agreement signed with Cai Litao. If the first-instance third party Cai Litao believes there is a dispute with Wang Qinjie, he may file a separate lawsuit, which does not affect the handling of this case. The Pledge Agreement held by Wang Qinjie did not contain the words "agree to this debt transfer"; they were unilaterally added by Licheng Company. Moreover, Wang Mouyu was not present when the agreement was signed. 3. Regarding the shareholders' capital contribution period, the period should be determined based on the records in the original documents of the Administration for Industry and Commerce, which are the only correct record. Since Guo Ruixing did not provide such evidence, her claim on this point should not be recognized.

Statement of the First-Instance Defendant Qu Yibo: He agreed with the appeal requests and the facts and reasons on which they were based from the appellants Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing. In addition, the case file showed that on December 30, 2015, the appellee Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company signed the Management Consulting Service Agreement. On November 22, 2017, Wang Qinjie and Cai Litao made a clear agreement on how to repay the RMB 650,000 loan involved and the security arrangements, which was signed by Wang Qinjie and confirmed by Licheng Company with its seal. Therefore, the original legal relationship had fundamentally changed after two years. The first-instance third party Cai Litao also provided jadeite jewelry as pledged property to Wang Qinjie in accordance with the Pledge Agreement, fulfilling his security obligation. Regarding the capital contribution period, he agreed with Guo Ruixing's opinion that the capital contribution period should expire on November 4, 2024. The first instance's finding that Qu Yibo failed to fully pay up his investment within the time frame and ordering him to bear liability was unfounded.

Statement of the First-Instance Third Party Cai Litao: Cai Litao did not appear in court and did not submit any statement.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

Additional findings: The shareholders of the Appellant Licheng Company at the time of its establishment in November 2015 were Wang and Yang; in May 2016, the shareholder was changed to Wang alone; on June 22, 2016, the shareholders were changed to Zhao and Guo Ruixing; and on August 22, 2016, the shareholders were changed again, and have since been Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo. The company registration records reflect that the articles of association of Licheng Company dated July 25, 2016, signed by Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo, provided that the capital contribution period for these two shareholders was to be December 31, 2018. As of the date of the second instance hearing, the enterprise credit information publicity report reflected that the capital contribution period for the shareholders Guo Ruixing and Qu Yibo of Licheng Company was November 4, 2045, with the publicity date being March 27, 2018. During the hearing, Guo Ruixing stated that he was unaware of the capital contribution period for the shareholders at the time of Licheng Company's establishment and whether it had been changed thereafter; he himself had not made any changes; he was merely a shareholder and not the legal representative of the company, and he was also unaware of any changes to the company's articles of association. Within the time limit designated by the court, Guo Ruixing failed to provide any documents such as the company's articles of association or a shareholders' resolution reflecting the change of the capital contribution period for the investors.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court opined in the second instance as follows:

1. The Appellee Wang Qinjie signed the *Management Consulting Service Agreement* with the Appellant Licheng Company, and the loan in question was also paid into Licheng Company. Regardless of who the shareholders or actual controller of Licheng Company were at the time the loan was made, this does not affect the contractual relationship between Wang Qinjie and Licheng Company. As for the agreement on the company's debts and claims made between the transferor and the transferee during the equity transfer process of Licheng Company, such agreement binds the parties thereto but cannot be used to oppose the company's creditors. Therefore, the ground of appeal by Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing that the court of first instance omitted the important party Wang is untenable.

2. The court of first instance, based on a comprehensive analysis of the content of the *Physical Property Pledge Agreement* and the formal differences between the copies of the *Physical Property Pledge Agreement* held by the Appellee Wang Qinjie and the third party at first instance, Cai Litao, concluded that the Appellant Licheng Company's assertion regarding the transfer of debt was not established. This conclusion is reasonable and lawful, and we will not repeat it here. Given that in this case Wang Qinjie is claiming the loan from Licheng Company and has not demanded repayment or exercised a security right from Cai Litao, the first instance court's determination that the pledge matters involved in the *Physical Property Pledge Agreement* are not within the scope of this case is not erroneous.

3. Regarding the liability of the Appellant Guo Ruixing. During the hearing, Guo Ruixing provided an enterprise credit information publicity report to prove that the capital contribution period for him as a shareholder of the Appellant Licheng Company had not yet expired. In response, the court of second instance holds that under the capital subscription system, although shareholders enjoy the benefit of the term by law, creditors also have legitimate expectations. The loan in question occurred in December 2015, with the maturity date being December 2016. At that time, the capital contribution period registered with the industrial and commercial authorities for the shareholders of Licheng Company was December 31, 2018. That is to say, in the event that Licheng Company failed to repay on time, the Appellee Wang Qinjie could reasonably expect to receive repayment from the shareholders' capital contributions upon the expiration of their contribution period in December 2018. Regardless of whether Guo Ruixing currently has evidence to prove that he handled the change of the capital contribution period through lawful and compliant means such as the company's articles of association, a shareholders' resolution, or otherwise, even if he did indeed handle such a change, since the change was made after the debt of Licheng Company arose and without the consent of the creditor, it substantively damages the creditor's legitimate expectations. Therefore, as a shareholder of Licheng Company, he cannot be exempted from liability on this ground. As for the voucher for Wang's transfer of RMB 5 million to Licheng Company, it is not an original document, its authenticity cannot be confirmed, and the voucher alone is insufficient to prove that the shareholder fulfilled its capital contribution obligation to the company. Accordingly, this evidence is not admitted. In summary, the appellate claims of Licheng Company and Guo Ruixing lack sufficient basis and are not supported. The first instance judgment has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and shall be affirmed.

In conclusion, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 6, 2019:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
